WP0-R1.title: fix WP0 review findings
acceptance: #1 In tests/unit/test_migration_0048_workflow_schema.py (RLS tests around lines 92-134 and the R4 delete tests around 307-378), add behavioural RLS and grant tests that run as the app role (mem_app), not as the pool owner. Cover three cases. Tenant A cannot SELECT or INSERT tenant B's rows in the new tables. UPDATE and DELETE are refused on workflow_stages, workflow_transitions and workflow_signoffs. A workflow that items or history still reference cannot be deleted. The current R4 delete tests run as the owner, so they would pass even without the grants.

#2 In the same test file, add constraint tests. Cover the partial unique index team_workflows_active_per_team (a second active workflow for the same team is rejected, while an inactive one is allowed). Cover unique (team_id, name). Cover the signoff_requests status CHECK (a bad value is rejected) and signoff_min >= 1 (0 is rejected). Cover the extended change_type CHECK (inserting 'stage', 'signoff_requested' and 'signoff_approved' succeeds, and a bogus value is rejected). Also assert that the partial unique index allows only one pending request per work item.

#3 In alembic/versions/0048_2026_10_17_team_workflows.py (downgrade, around lines 276-290), add a comment saying the downgrade fails if stage, signoff_requested or signoff_approved history rows exist. Add a downgrade/upgrade round-trip test on an empty schema (the plan's NOTES promise one).

WP1-R1.title: fix WP1 review findings
acceptance: #1 src/mem_mcp/mindmap/work_items.py:809 and workflow_moves.py:315: nothing writes work_items.workflow_id on a move or commit, so it stays NULL. The `workflow_id IS NOT NULL` routing in set_work_item_status and set_work_item_kind never fires, and a legacy set_status can then skip sign-off. Set workflow_id (resolved via _resolve_workflow) when an item moves or commits. Add a test: after a gated move, set_status must still enforce the gate.

#2 src/mem_mcp/mindmap/work_items.py:628: mark_work_item must route through move_work_item, as wp1.md and the T3 acceptance list require. set_work_item_status must also not ignore the sign-off proposal result. A gated move must raise MoveBlockedError instead of silently returning the unchanged item. Add tests for both paths.

#3 src/mem_mcp/mindmap/workflow_moves.py:446: the signatory team-membership check runs only when signoff_roles is set. When it is empty, any tenant member can sign. Always require the signatory to be a team member resolved through team_role_assignments, and to be someone other than the owner when the rule demands it. Add a test for a non-member signing.

#4 src/mem_mcp/mindmap/workflow_moves.py:398 and :586: the move-request lookup filters on tenant_id only, never on team_id. A request can be signed or cancelled through the wrong team context. Add team_id to both lookups and add a cross-team test.

#5 src/mem_mcp/mindmap/workflow_moves.py:509 and :318: the commit UPDATE requires current_stage = from_stage. For legacy items current_stage is NULL and the stage comes from status, so 0 rows match. Line 542 then marks the request committed anyway. Handle the legacy NULL current_stage case by matching on status or coalescing. Check the rowcount and raise instead of marking the request committed when the item did not advance. Add a legacy-item commit test.

wps.title: Migration — workflow schema + history extensions (legacy materialisation deferred to WP1, no backfill)

da_goal_notes: R3 says sign-off from someone other than the OWNER, but the rules exclude only the PROPOSER. Pick one: exclude both the item owner and the proposer, and state it in WP1.; R6 'waiting on you' has no read path. Add a pending-signoffs-for-me query to WP1, plus an MCP tool and a web endpoint, so the board and agents show the same list.; allowed_moves and blocked_reason are only read from the move response, so the board can't show them before a move is tried. WP1 needs a read function that returns them per item, and WP2 and WP3 need to expose it, including in work_list and the board list.; Backfill and legacy-workflow materialisation are ambiguous: the goal says both 'first reference' (lazy) and 'backfill existing rows' (in the migration). Choose one. Lazy materialisation is simpler and safe, and WP0 should state which one it does.; The set_work_item_status routing for workflowed items appears only under Risks. Put it in WP1/WP2 as a deliverable with a test in WP5, so sign-off can't be bypassed.
